# Draft:Mamoun Abu Nowar

----
Mamoun Abu-Nowar (born 6 January 1950) is a retired officer of the Royal Jordanian Air Force (RJAF) and a military analyst. He served in operational, command, instructional, and senior staff positions in the RJAF and retired in 2000 with the rank of major general. Following his military career, he became active as a commentator and analyst on defense and security affairs, with his analysis appearing in major regional and international media, including Al Jazeera, the BBC, and Sky News, among others.
Early life and education
Abu-Nowar was born in Amman on 6 January 1950. After completing high school, he joined the Royal Jordanian Air Force as a cadet on 15 October 1968 and was sent to the Pakistan Air Force Academy in Risalpur. He completed basic pilot training there and graduated in January 1971, when he was commissioned as a second lieutenant in the RJAF.
During his career, Abu-Nowar completed a wide range of professional military education and specialist training in several countries. His training included basic pilot training at the Pakistan Air Force Academy in 1968, the Instructor Pilot Course at the United States Air Force’s Randolph Air Force Base in 1975, and the Fighter Weapons Instructor Course at USAF William Air Force Base in September 1977. He also attended a simulated air defense planning course in the United Kingdom in 1979, the Squadron Officer School at USAF Maxwell Air Force Base in 1981, the Squadron Supervisory Course with the Royal Air Force in 1984, and the RAF Staff College at Bracknell in 1986. In 1994, he completed senior-level professional education at the United States Air Force Air University’s Air War College.
In 1995, Abu-Nowar earned a master’s degree in political science from Auburn University at Montgomery in the United States. He also completed a master’s degree in military science.
Notable training incident
While undergoing pilot training at the Pakistan Air Force Academy, Abu-Nowar was involved in a serious T-37 aircraft accident. During a formation training flight near Peshawar, his aircraft collided with another, lost control, and caught fire. He ejected safely using the aircraft’s ejection seat and survived the crash, later recounting the experience in an interview with a Jordanian news agency.
Military career
Abu-Nowar served in the Royal Jordanian Air Force for more than three decades, holding a variety of operational, command, and senior staff appointments. As a fighter pilot, he flew the Hawker Hunter, Northrop F-5, and Dassault Mirage F-1, as well as training aircraft including the T-37, T-33, and T-38. Over the course of his career, he accumulated more than 2,900 flight hours.
Following his initial training, he served as an operational and instructor pilot on Hawker Hunter aircraft with No. 1 Squadron. In 1974, he became an instructor pilot on the F-5 with No. 2 Squadron at King Hussein Air College. In 1977, he was appointed flight commander of No. 9 Squadron flying the F-5 at Prince Hassan Air Base.
In 1981, Abu-Nowar served as chief representative of fighter pilots in the RJAF study group. He later commanded No. 2 Squadron on the F-5 at King Hussein Air College. In 1985, he was assigned as a staff officer in the planning and operational branch at the Directorate of Air Operations. The following year, he commanded No. 1 Squadron operating the Mirage F-1 at Salti Air Base.
In 1990, he was appointed Officer Commanding the Flying Wing at King Faisal Air Base. In 1992, he served as military secretary to His Royal Highness Prince Hassan of Jordan. In 1993, he became chief instructor pilot at King Hussein Air College, and in 1995 he was appointed base commander at King Faisal Air Base.
In 1997, Abu-Nowar became director of air reconnaissance at RJAF headquarters, and in 1999 he was appointed director of the Studies Department at RJAF headquarters. He retired from active service in 2000 with the rank of major general.
Awards and decorations
During his service, Abu-Nowar received several Jordanian and foreign military decorations, including the Order of Al-Nahda (Second Class), the Order of Al-Kawkab (Third Class), the Order of Al-Istiqlal (Fourth Class), the Order of Al-Istihqaq (Third Class), and the Egyptian Istihqaq (Fifth Class).
Post-military career, media, and research
After retiring from the Royal Jordanian Air Force in 2000, Abu-Nowar has worked for more than 25 years as a military and strategic analyst. His commentary on regional and international security issues has been published and broadcast by major international news organizations such as BBC, Reuters, Al Jazeera, Deutsche Welle, Sky News, France 24, TRT, and CGTN, among others. His analysis has addressed military operations, air power, regional security dynamics, and the strategic implications of armed conflicts.
In addition to his broadcast work, Abu-Nowar has contributed written analysis and research on defense and security affairs, with his work published internationally. His writing has examined modern warfare, air operations, regional conflicts, and the strategic and political dimensions of military force.
Beyond media and publications, Abu-Nowar has also participated in policy- and research-oriented work in the field of international security. Through his involvement with international research and analysis institutions, including the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, he has contributed to think-tank-level discussions on military and strategic issues, reflecting his continued engagement in defense and security analysis after his military career.
